name: Alexander of Aetolia
bio: Alexander of Aetolia is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 3rd century BC.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 709).

poems.title: Book VII, 709
poems.author: Alexander of Aetolia
poems.text: Ancient Sardis, home of my fathers, had I been reared in thee I would have been a cernus-bearer or eunuch, wearing ornaments of gold and beating pretty tambourines; but now my name is Aleman, and I am a citizen of Sparta of the many tripods, and have learnt to know the Heliconian Muses who made me greater than the tyrants Dascyles and Gyges.
